newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK mortgage at HSBC HK Bank slows.
newsitem.headline: HK mortgage at HSBC HK Bank slows.

text.p: HSBC Holdings Plc's Hongkong and Shanghai Banking Corp Ltd (Hongkong Bank) said on Tuesday its Hong Kong mortgage business had slowed slightly after a recent correction in the property market.
"I think that since there has been this correction, it has slowed down a bit," John Strickland, chairman of Hongkong Bank, told reporters.
But he said the mortgage slowdown was "not a serious problem".
Hong Kong property prices have tumbled some 10 percent from their recent peaks since late March when the government announced measures to curb sharply rising prices.
Strickland said Hong Kong's property market was consolidating, with prices now at the upper limit of affordability.
He said the market consolidation was good.

"Prices would probably get into unaffordable levels with the rate at which it is accelerating. And therefore some modest correction is in fact entirely good for Hong Kong and good for the house buyers," he said.
Asked if banks were likely to lower mortgage rates this year, he said: "I would have thought they would."
He said if banks further reduced mortgage rates that would be due to competition rather than property market downturn.
On interest margin for mortgage loans, he said: "If it's going to move in any direction, it's going to move down."
